original_question: Characterize all connected signed graphs whose adjacency spectrum consists of exactly two distinct eigenvalues.
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Problem 3.9 ("Signed graphs with exactly 2 distinct eigenvalues"): "Characterize all connected signed graphs whose spectrum consists of two distinct eigenvalues."
correct_elements: Your draft is already essentially the paper’s exact target. It correctly asks for a characterization, keeps the connected signed-graph setting, and isolates the precise spectral condition of having exactly two distinct eigenvalues. Your phrase "adjacency spectrum" is faithful to the paper’s intent, since the paper fixes adjacency spectrum as the default notion of spectrum in the sequel.
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, the object should be defined as a finite signed graph Γ=(G,σ), where G=(V,E) is the underlying graph and σ:E→{+1,-1} is the signature.
The operator whose spectrum is being studied should be stated explicitly: the adjacency matrix A(Γ), the symmetric {0,+1,-1}-matrix with A_{ij}=σ(ij) when ij is an edge and A_{ij}=0 otherwise.
The ambient field is implicitly the real numbers: A(Γ) is a real symmetric matrix, so the eigenvalues are real.
The paper presents this as an open classification problem in Section 3.2; it does not add extra hypotheses such as regularity, cyclotomicity, bounded degree, or a signed-diameter condition.
The paper does not explicitly bake an equivalence relation into Problem 3.9, so a refined stand-alone version should not insert "up to switching isomorphism" unless that is declared separately.
There are no homogeneity, polynomial-degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic "for all sufficiently large m" conditions in this problem.
refined_question: Let Γ=(G,σ) be a finite connected signed graph, where σ:E(G)→{+1,-1}, and let A(Γ) be its adjacency matrix, i.e. the symmetric {0,+1,-1}-matrix with A_{ij}=σ(ij) when ij∈E(G) and A_{ij}=0 otherwise. Characterize all such signed graphs Γ for which A(Γ) has exactly two distinct real eigenvalues.
justification: The draft is aiming at Section 3.2, Problem 3.9, and in fact is almost verbatim to the paper’s official formulation. The nearby context shows that the paper is working with adjacency spectra by default, after defining signed graphs and their adjacency matrices in the Introduction. The surrounding discussion in Section 3.2 gives examples and related consequences—such as maximal cyclotomic signed graphs in Theorem 3.8 and the signed-diameter bound in Theorem 3.10—but these do not replace Problem 3.9 with a sharper equivalent statement. So the faithful refinement is simply the same problem made fully self-contained by spelling out Γ=(G,σ) and A(Γ), without broadening it to other few-eigenvalue, cyclotomic, or diameter-based problems.
